item.title: Miss MHCC & Carpenters Tower Sala Korosaya crowned Miss Hibiscus 2026
item.description: Temalesi Vono , Antornette Vuniuca · 05/09/2026 Miss MHCC & Carpenters Tower Sala Korosaya has been crowned Miss Hibiscus 2026, taking the coveted title at the FMF Hibiscus Festival in Suva tonight.
item.content:encoded:
Temalesi Vono , Antornette Vuniuca · 05/09/2026

Miss MHCC & Carpenters Tower Sala Korosaya has been crowned Miss Hibiscus 2026, taking the coveted title at the FMF Hibiscus Festival in Suva tonight.

For Korosaya, entering the festival was never simply about winning a crown.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Korosaya says her main goal was to challenge herself while developing her speaking and leadership skills.

Korosaya says the journey was not without its challenges,admitting she was often hard on herself and had to learn to give herself grace when things did not go as planned.

She says there were also a few wardrobe malfunctions along the way, but the support of her team helped her get through the difficult moments and put the pieces back together.

Now wearing the Hibiscus crown, Korosaya has her sights set on the next chapter.

She plans to complete her double degree before moving on to USP and hopes to eventually represent the Pacific Islands.

The Hibiscus queen also took out the Best Talent award earlier this week.

Her victory brings the 70th FMF Hibiscus Festival to a spectacular close, with thousands gathering to witness the crowning of the new Hibiscus Queen.

Meanwhile, Miss Fiji Rugby Union Suliana Latianara has been crowned 1st runner-up, while Miss Superstore Nicole Matavesi was named 2nd runner-up.

item.title: Online Safety Commission receives 960 complaints this year, 65% relate to cyberbullying
item.description: Speaking during the fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan, Commissioner Filipe Batiwale says most of these complaints are being reviewed and assessed, while some have been closed off. He says most of the cases received involve requests for electronic communications or social media posts to be taken down.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking during the fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan, Commissioner Filipe Batiwale says most of these complaints are being reviewed and assessed, while some have been closed off.

He says most of the cases received involve requests for electronic communications or social media posts to be taken down.

Batiwale says cyberbullying involves electronic communication being used in a way that causes harm or serious emotional distress to another person.

He adds a number of complaints remain unresolved, with one of the major issues being that complainants fail to properly complete and sign the required complaint form.

He says under the current framework, a person making a complaint to the Online Safety Commission is required to complete a form, including providing a signature, as required under the Online Safety Act regulations.

Batiwale says this requirement is sometimes overlooked by complainants and is a major drawback when dealing with complaints received by the Commission.

He says complaints can also involve people being concerned about material posted online about themselves, their relatives or other people concerned.

However, Batiwale says the Commission's current legal framework restricts its ability to assist when the online content is completely unrelated to the person making the complaint.

item.title: Teachers say sign language, braille should take priority over Chinese
item.description: A group of teachers are calling on the Government to prioritise the introduction of sign language and Braille in Fiji’s mainstream curriculum instead of introducing Chinese language, saying students should be equipped with inclusive communication skills from an early age. The teachers, who have requested anonymity and teach in the Suva area, say sign language and Braille should be taught from Year
item.content:encoded:
A group of teachers are calling on the Government to prioritise the introduction of sign language and Braille in Fiji’s mainstream curriculum instead of introducing Chinese language, saying students should be equipped with inclusive communication skills from an early age.

The teachers, who have requested anonymity and teach in the Suva area, say sign language and Braille should be taught from Year 1 through to Year 13 to help create a more inclusive education system.

Speaking to fijivillage News, they say the recent USP sign language incident has highlighted the need for greater awareness and understanding of people living with disabilities.

They say while there is ongoing discussion about inclusivity and ensuring people with disabilities are fully included in society, more practical measures are needed within the education system to make this a reality.

The teachers say communication remains one of the major barriers faced by people who are deaf, hard of hearing, blind or visually impaired, particularly when accessing employment opportunities and participating in workplaces.

They believe teaching sign language and Braille to all students, rather than limiting these skills to specialised programmes, could help break down communication barriers and build greater understanding from an early age.

The teachers say universities already have students studying special and inclusive education, and the Government could consider creating opportunities for suitably qualified graduates to be placed in schools to teach sign language, Braille and other inclusive communication skills.

They say this could also create employment opportunities for graduates while strengthening inclusive education within primary and secondary schools.

The teachers further suggest that secondary schools could introduce students to assistive technology used by blind and visually impaired people, allowing them to better understand how technology can support people with disabilities in education, employment and everyday life.

They say if students are exposed to these skills throughout their school years, they could eventually enter universities and workplaces with a greater ability to communicate and interact with people with disabilities.

The teachers believe this could contribute towards creating more inclusive workplaces in Fiji and reducing communication barriers faced by people with disabilities when seeking employment.

They are calling on the Government to consider practical initiatives that directly benefit Fiji’s children and communities when reviewing future changes to the national curriculum.

They also want greater discussion on whether sign language, Braille and disability awareness should become a core part of mainstream education in Fiji.

item.title: SJSS marks 70 Years of empowering women with week-long platinum jubilee beginning tomorrow.
item.description: Saint Joseph’s Secondary School is set to celebrate a historic milestone this week as it marks 70 years of educating and empowering women through a week-long Platinum Jubilee celebration beginning tomorrow. The celebrations will bring together past and present students, staff, and members of the wider school community for a programme filled with faith, culture, sisterhood, reflection and celebrati
item.content:encoded:
Saint Joseph’s Secondary School is set to celebrate a historic milestone this week as it marks 70 years of educating and empowering women through a week-long Platinum Jubilee celebration beginning tomorrow.

The celebrations will bring together past and present students, staff, and members of the wider school community for a programme filled with faith, culture, sisterhood, reflection and celebration.

The Platinum Jubilee officially begins tomorrow with an Opening Mass at 10am at Mt St Mary’s Church.

The celebrations continue on Monday, September 7, with a morning fitness session at Zenergy Gym, followed by a welcome cocktail at the SJSS Hall at 5pm.

On Tuesday, September 8, the programme will feature a Law and Governance Breakfast at 8.30am at the Fiji Museum Café, followed by a visit to State House at Government House at 11am.

The evening will continue at the SJSS Hall from 6pm, with organisers promising an unforgettable evening of culture, laughter, sisterhood and music.

Wednesday, September 9, will begin with a morning walk at 7am, starting from the Suva Bowling Club and ending at the Nasese Seafront .

A post-walk breakfast will follow at 8.30am, hosted by the SJSS Alumnae medics, with a timely discussion on body autonomy .

The evening will feature a Flower Power Tekiteki Night at Paradiso Restaurant from 5pm, followed by an Island Night at the Suva Bowling Club at 6.30pm.

On Thursday, September 10, alumnae and guests will have the opportunity to explore the city during a Bus Tour of Old Suva, departing from Albert Park at 10am.

A prefects’ school tour will be held at 1pm, before the day concludes with the Bold and Beautiful 90s Quiz and Disco at 5pm at the Fiji Museum Deck.

Friday, September 11, will be the Jubilee Celebration Day, beginning at 9am at the SJSS School Hall.

The day will continue with a Pure Fiji tour and shopping experience at 12.30pm, followed by the SJSS Alumnae March at 3pm at the SJSS Sports Field.

The Platinum Legacy Cocktail and Fashion Show will then take centre stage at 6pm at the Fiji Museum Deck.

Next Saturday, will celebrate the diversity and richness of the Pacific with Pacific Market Day from 9.30am at the SJSS School Hall.

The celebrations will reach one of their major highlights that evening with the Pacific Elegance Gala at 6pm at the Vodafone Arena.

The week-long milestone will conclude on Sunday, September 13, with a Closing Mass at 1pm at Sacred Heart Cathedral.

item.title: Ratu Semi installed as 5th Tui Yakete in traditional ceremony
item.description: Ratu Semi Vukivukinavanua Lotawa Nadakaibitu has been traditionally installed as the fifth Tui Yakete following a traditional ceremony at the Vatu ni Veibuli in Nalotawa Village in the highlands of Ba. The 36-year-old, Ratu Semi, was installed following the traditional yaqona ceremony and has also been formally recognised by the relevant government authorities.
item.content:encoded:
Ratu Semi Vukivukinavanua Lotawa Nadakaibitu has been traditionally installed as the fifth Tui Yakete following a traditional ceremony at the Vatu ni Veibuli in Nalotawa Village in the highlands of Ba.

The 36-year-old, Ratu Semi, was installed following the traditional yaqona ceremony and has also been formally recognised by the relevant government authorities.

A religious blessing was also conducted following the traditional ceremonies.

The installation was significant as Ratu Semi was seated at the traditional foundation established by the elders of the vanua, where the Tui Yakete is traditionally installed.

Ratu Semi was traditionally dressed at Namaravulevu before being escorted by the Sauturaga and his Bati to the Vatu ni Veibuli, where he drank the ceremonial yaqona prepared for him.

A tabua was also presented to Ratu Semi as part of the traditional ceremony entrusting the land, waters and people of Yakete into his care.

In his first address to the people of the vanua, Ratu Semi expressed his gratitude for the significant effort and preparations undertaken for his installation into the chiefly position.

He assured the people that he would carry out his responsibilities to the best of his ability to ensure peace and wellbeing within the vanua of Yakete.

Ratu Semi is the fifth Tui Yakete to be traditionally installed.

The previous installation was held in 2009 when his father, Ratu Savenaca Tiqe Nadakaibitu, was installed as Tui Yakete .

The Tikina of Yakete includes the villages of Nalotawa, Yaloku, Rara, Nanuku, Tukuraki, Tabataba and Naivilawa.

item.title: Paddle for Hope reaches Tagage Village on Day 5, pushes fight against single-use plastics
item.description: The Paddle for Hope team has reached Tagage Village on Day 5 of its more than 500-kilometre journey around Viti Levu, taking with them a message that protecting Fiji's ocean begins with the actions people take in their homes and communities. The Paddle for Hope started its journey from the National Sailing Centre in Suva, travelling to the Suva Foreshore, before continuing to Muaivuso.
item.content:encoded:
The Paddle for Hope team has reached Tagage Village on Day 5 of its more than 500-kilometre journey around Viti Levu, taking with them a message that protecting Fiji's ocean begins with the actions people take in their homes and communities.

The Paddle for Hope started its journey from the National Sailing Centre in Suva, travelling to the Suva Foreshore, before continuing to Muaivuso.

The team was in Togoru and Navua on Day 2 of its journey before heading to Rovadrau, the Pearl Resort and Lomary on Day 3.

The team was in Galoa and Navutulevu yesterday, where they were welcomed by villagers and given an opportunity to explain how single-use plastics can enter the food chain and potentially affect people's health and wellbeing.

The team also thanked the people of Navutulevu Village for their hospitality and for providing a platform to share the message behind the campaign.

This is part of the SUP Against SUP initiative, which stands for Stand Up Paddling Against Single-Use Plastics, and uses the Paddle for Hope journey to promote cleaner oceans and healthier communities.

The Ministry of Environment also delivered a presentation during the visit, focusing on recycling and waste management.

The Paddle for Hope team says the journey continues to encourage communities to reduce their reliance on single-use plastics and take greater responsibility for protecting the environment.

item.title: No one charged yet in alleged overseas employment scam involving more than 300 Fijians
item.description: Crystal Robanakadavu · 04/09/2026 Police had earlier confirmed to fijivillage News that a report has been lodged at the Namaka Police Station and an investigation is underway.
item.content:encoded:
Crystal Robanakadavu · 04/09/2026

Police had earlier confirmed to fijivillage News that a report has been lodged at the Namaka Police Station and an investigation is underway.

More than 300 people claim they paid $100 each after being promised overseas employment opportunities, with some expecting to travel to Australia.

They say over 50 people reportedly turned up at the Nadi International Airport last Saturday expecting to travel overseas but later discovered that there were no flight bookings for them.

Some of those affected had reportedly resigned from their jobs in preparation for the promised overseas employment.

The Ministry of Employment is urging those affected to lodge reports with Police and stresses that workers are not required to pay recruitment fees to participate in Government-facilitated overseas employment programmes.
